chapters.title: Three Writing Systems in One Doorway
chapters.label: ch:ja-three-scripts
chapters.canDo: I can greet someone in the daytime, answer yes or no, and thank them politely, reading each word in the script Japanese actually uses for it.

payoff.summary: A six-line daytime doorway exchange that mixes hiragana and kanji and uses no untaught word.

chapters.title: Eight Signs, and Three Words You Can Read
chapters.label: ch:ja-hiragana-eight
chapters.canDo: I can write eight hiragana signs from memory and read the daytime greeting and both yes-or-no answers by sounding out their signs in order, including the sign that is pronounced wa because it is a topic marker.

payoff.summary: The daytime greeting assembled from five signs the reader can each write from memory, introducing nothing new — including the one read wa because it is a topic marker rather than the sign for that sound.
